title: Investigations of Massive Filaments and Star Formation (INFANT). I. Core Identification and Core Mass Function
question: Identify dense cores in ALMA 1.3 mm maps of 8 massive filamentary clouds, classify them as prestellar or protostellar, compare getsf and astrodendro, and derive core masses and the core mass function (CMF) and how it changes with cloud evolution

recipe.goal: calibrate and image the 1.3 mm continuum
recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, line-free continuum visibilities, tclean multiscale mosaic imaging

recipe.goal: identify cores and measure sizes and flux densities with getsf
recipe.method: getsf extraction on the non-primary-beam-corrected 1.3 mm images; fluxes then primary-beam corrected; catalogue cut with the recommended optimal selection criteria
key_parameters: selection includes aspect ratio below 2, peak and integrated flux S/N above 2

recipe.goal: estimate 90% completeness by artificial core insertion
recipe.method: Insert synthetic beam-shaped cores into the image, rerun getsf, count recoveries
key_parameters: 10 cores per experiment, 10 repetitions per flux
assumptions: inserted cores have the same shape as the synthesized beam (unresolved limit)

recipe.goal: measure core gas temperatures from VLA NH3
recipe.method: Average NH3 (1,1) and (2,2) spectra within the getsf FWHM of each core, fitted with an LTE model
key_parameters: fit only if (1,1) detected above 4 sigma and (2,2) above 2.5 sigma; 125 of 183 cores qualify
free parameters: velocity, rotational temperature, NH3 column density, velocity dispersion
assumptions: uniform filling factor of 1 for all transitions and hyperfine components

recipe.goal: convert 1.3 mm flux densities to core gas masses
recipe.method: Optically thin isothermal dust emission, M = d^2 F / (kappa B(T)), multiplied by 100 for gas
assumptions: dust temperature equal to the NH3 gas temperature; region median used where NH3 temperature is unavailable

recipe.goal: classify cores as prestellar or protostellar
recipe.method: Protostellar if associated with a molecular outflow or compact warm-core emission (H2CO 3(2,2)-2(2,1), 3(2,1)-2(2,0), CH3OH 4(2,2)-3(1,2)); otherwise prestellar candidate
key_parameters: warm core: peak above 4 sigma in any of three lines, with centrally peaked compact morphology
assumptions: outflow-based count is a lower limit because outflows near the plane of sky are missed

recipe.method: Run both on the same maps, repeat the artificial-core insertion for detection rate and flux recovery
key_parameters: astrodendro: base flux density threshold 4 sigma, minimum significance 1 sigma, minimum area half the synthesized beam
assumptions: comparison concerns detecting point-like sources in a 2-D map

recipe.goal: test whether protostellar cores are more massive than prestellar cores
recipe.method: Single-sided Mann-Whitney U test on 1.3 mm flux density and mass, for all clouds and for young and evolved groups
key_parameters: null hypothesis: protostellar flux or mass is equal or smaller than prestellar
assumptions: sample is flux limited; temperature needed to convert flux to mass; prestellar cores probably under-counted at low mass

recipe.goal: fit the high-mass slope of the core mass function
recipe.method: Maximum likelihood power-law fit of dN/dlogM above 1.5 Msun for all cores, prestellar cores, and young and evolved cloud groups
key_parameters: young group: I18308, I18337, I18460; evolved group: I18530, I19074, I19220 (L/M plus other indicators)
assumptions: masses use NH3 temperatures (see step 5); completeness 0.53-0.89 Msun at 15 K, 1.0-1.5 Msun at 10 K

recipe.method: alpha = 5 sigma^2 R / (G M) with NH3 line width (channel width subtracted, thermal part removed) and deconvolved radius
key_parameters: minimum deconvolved size of half the beam; critical alpha = 2

score_reason: The ALMA project code and imaging parameters (robust, scales, pixel size) and the getsf setup are given, and results are numeric, but calibrator and mask details are missing and the temperatures and outflow classifications depend on VLA and companion-paper steps that are not reproducible from this paper
rediscovery_reason: ALMA data come from a single listed Cycle 5 project in the archive, the continuum imaging and getsf core extraction are specified, and the outputs (183 cores, mass and CMF slopes) are numeric; a continuum-only redo with a fixed temperature is feasible even though NH3 temperatures and outflow classes are not
